name: FIToFICustomerCreditTransfer
label: FI to FI Customer Credit Transfer
summary: Moves a customer credit transfer between financial institutions. This is the interbank leg of what a customer kicked off with a pain.001 — the message that actually carries the money across the correspondent or clearing chain.
whenUsed: The workhorse of cross-border and high-value domestic payments, and the direct replacement for MT103. At least one party to the transfer is a non-financial customer; if both debtor and creditor are financial institutions you want pacs.009 instead. Sent by the debtor agent to the next agent in the chain, then forwarded agent to agent until it reaches the creditor agent. Each hop re-wraps the same transaction, so the same payment exists as several pacs.008 messages with different instructing and instructed agents but one stable UETR and End To End Id.
gotchas: Interbank Settlement Amount is what settles between the agents; Instructed Amount is what the debtor asked to send. They differ once charges or FX are applied, and confusing them produces reconciliation breaks that only surface at month end.
ChargeBearer must agree with what the debtor actually agreed to. SHAR with an unexpected intermediary deduction is the single most common customer complaint in correspondent banking.

Unstructured address lines are being withdrawn across schemes. Writing to AdrLine instead of the structured StrtNm/TwnNm/Ctry elements is technically valid base ISO and will still be rejected by CBPR+.

fields.name: Group Header
fields.note: Exactly one per message, describing the batch as a whole.

fields.name: Message Identification
fields.note: Assigned by the sender and must be unique for that sender, usually per day. Receiving agents use it for duplicate detection, so never reuse one after a failed send — fix and resend with a new id. Max 35 characters.

fields.name: Creation Date Time
fields.note: When the message was created, not when the payment executes. ISO date-time with offset, e.g. 2026-10-10T09:30:47+11:00.

fields.name: Number Of Transactions
fields.note: Count of CdtTrfTxInf blocks. Must match exactly — a mismatch is a hard schema-level rejection, not a warning. CBPR+ pins this to 1, one payment per message.

fields.name: Control Sum
fields.note: Sum of all instructed amounts, currency-agnostic. A checksum for the receiver, not an instruction.

fields.name: Total Interbank Settlement Amount
fields.note: Only meaningful when every transaction settles in the same currency.

fields.name: Interbank Settlement Date
fields.note: Group-level settlement date. If present here it applies to all transactions; most implementations set it per transaction instead.

fields.name: Settlement Information
fields.note: How the interbank leg settles. The chosen method constrains which other elements in this block are allowed.

fields.name: Settlement Method
fields.note: CLRG for clearing systems, INDA/INGA for nostro/vostro accounts, COVE when a separate cover payment settles it.

fields.name: Clearing System
fields.note: Required in practice when SettlementMethod is CLRG — names the system, e.g. TARGET2, NPP, FEDNET.

fields.name: Clearing System Code
fields.note: An ExternalCashClearingSystem1Code value. Distinct from the clearing-system codes used for member identifiers — same idea, different published list.

fields.name: Settlement Account
fields.note: The nostro or vostro account being settled across, when the method is INDA or INGA.

fields.name: Instructing Reimbursement Agent
fields.note: Agent through which the instructing agent reimburses, in a cover arrangement.

fields.name: Instructed Reimbursement Agent
fields.note: The mirror of the above on the instructed side.

fields.name: Third Reimbursement Agent
fields.note: A third institution in the reimbursement arrangement, where the two agents share no direct account relationship.

fields.name: Instructing Agent
fields.note: The agent sending this particular hop. Changes at every hop — this is the element that tells you where in the chain a copy of the payment came from.

fields.name: Instructed Agent
fields.note: The agent receiving this hop. Also changes per hop.

fields.name: Credit Transfer Transaction Information
fields.note: One block per payment. Repeating in base ISO, but most schemes — CBPR+ included — restrict it to exactly one so that a rejection cannot partially fail a batch.

fields.name: Payment Identification
fields.note: The set of references that let this payment be tracked and matched. Four different ids with four different lifetimes — worth getting straight once.

fields.name: Instruction Identification
fields.note: Point-to-point reference between this instructing agent and this instructed agent only. Replaced at every hop, so never use it to correlate end to end.

fields.name: End To End Identification
fields.note: The debtor's own reference, carried unchanged to the creditor. This is what the creditor reconciles against. Mandatory; if the debtor supplied nothing, senders conventionally put the literal NOTPROVIDED.

fields.name: Transaction Identification
fields.note: Reference assigned by the first instructing agent, intended to stay stable across the chain. In practice superseded by UETR.

fields.name: UETR
fields.note: Unique End-to-end Transaction Reference — a UUID v4 that survives every hop, return and cancellation. Optional in base ISO, mandatory under CBPR+, and the key that makes SWIFT gpi tracking work. Generate it once at origination and never alter it.

fields.name: Clearing System Reference
fields.note: Reference assigned by the clearing system itself.

fields.name: Payment Type Information
fields.note: How the payment should be handled: priority, scheme, instrument, purpose category.

fields.name: Instruction Priority
fields.note: A hint only. Most clearing systems ignore it in favour of Service Level.

fields.name: Service Level
fields.note: The rulebook the payment runs under. This is the binding scheme marker — SEPA validation starts here.

fields.name: Local Instrument
fields.note: Scheme-specific product. Read it against the relevant rulebook — the same code can mean different things in different schemes.

fields.name: Category Purpose
fields.note: Why the payment is made, at a level agents may act on — can affect routing and cut-offs. Contrast with Purpose further down, which agents must leave alone.

fields.name: Interbank Settlement Amount
fields.note: The amount that actually moves between the agents, with its currency as an attribute: <IntrBkSttlmAmt Ccy="AUD">1500.00</IntrBkSttlmAmt>. This is the settlement figure — not necessarily what the debtor asked to send.

fields.name: Interbank Settlement Date
fields.note: Value date for the interbank leg. Must be a business day for the settlement currency; getting this wrong triggers a DT01 rejection.

fields.name: Settlement Time Indication
fields.note: Reports when settlement actually occurred, debit and credit timestamps.

fields.name: Settlement Time Request
fields.note: Asks for settlement by a given time (CLSTime, TillTime, FromTime, RejectTime).

fields.name: Instructed Amount
fields.note: What the debtor instructed, in the original currency, before charges and FX. Present whenever it differs from the settlement amount — which is exactly when it matters.

fields.name: Exchange Rate
fields.note: The rate applied between instructed and settlement currency.

fields.name: Charge Bearer
fields.note: Who pays the fees. Mandatory. CBPR+ allows only DEBT, CRED and SHAR; SLEV is for scheme-governed payments like SEPA.

fields.name: Charges Information
fields.note: An audit trail of charges already taken, one entry per agent that deducted. Repeating, and it grows as the payment travels — this is how a creditor can see why less money arrived.

fields.name: Charging Agent
fields.note: Which agent took this charge.

fields.name: Previous Instructing Agent 1
fields.note: Preserves the agent chain already traversed, up to three levels.

fields.name: Intermediary Agent 1
fields.note: Next agent after the debtor agent. Up to three intermediaries can be named, in order.

fields.name: Debtor
fields.note: Whose account is debited. Mandatory as a block, but note that every element inside it is individually optional in base ISO — which is why schemes have to layer their own requirements on top.

fields.name: Debtor Name
fields.note: Optional in base ISO, mandatory under every real scheme and under FATF Recommendation 16. Max 140 characters.

fields.name: Debtor Postal Address
fields.note: The focus of the industry-wide structured-address migration. Use the discrete elements below rather than AdrLine.

fields.name: Town Name
fields.note: Together with Country, the minimum a hybrid address needs.

fields.name: Country Sub Division
fields.note: State, province or territory — e.g. VIC.

fields.name: Country
fields.note: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, e.g. AU. The one address element schemes almost always require.

fields.name: Address Line
fields.note: Free-text address lines. Still schema-valid, but being withdrawn — CBPR+ forbids it for the debtor and creditor from the November 2026 release. Treat new use as a defect.

fields.name: Debtor Identification
fields.note: Choice of organisation id or private-person id — exactly one, never both.

fields.name: Any BIC
fields.note: The debtor's own BIC, where it has one. Not the agent's BIC.

fields.name: LEI
fields.note: 20-character Legal Entity Identifier. Increasingly used for corporate payments reporting.

fields.name: Private Identification
fields.note: Date and place of birth, or an other-id scheme such as a passport number.

fields.name: Debtor Account
fields.note: Optional at base-ISO level because a payment can be funded without a named account; mandatory under most schemes.

fields.name: Account Identification
fields.note: A choice: IBAN or Other. Never both.

fields.name: IBAN
fields.note: Mandatory in IBAN countries; must be used in preference to Other where an IBAN exists.

fields.name: Other Account Identification
fields.note: For non-IBAN countries — Australian BSB plus account number, US account numbers, and so on.

fields.name: Debtor Agent
fields.note: The debtor's bank. Mandatory.

fields.name: BICFI
fields.note: The agent's BIC, 8 or 11 characters. Renamed from BIC in earlier versions — code written against pacs.008.001.02 will be looking for the wrong tag.

fields.name: Clearing System Member Identification
fields.note: How a domestic sort code, BSB or routing number travels in ISO 20022.

fields.name: Member Identification
fields.note: The actual code — e.g. 083004 for an Australian BSB.

fields.name: Creditor Agent
fields.note: The creditor's bank.

fields.name: Member Identification
fields.note: The creditor agent's domestic routing code — ABA routing number, BSB, sort code. Domestic schemes route on this rather than on BIC.

fields.name: Creditor
fields.note: Who gets paid.

fields.name: Creditor Name
fields.note: Optional in base ISO, required by every scheme and by sanctions screening. Max 140 characters.

fields.name: Address Line
fields.note: Same withdrawal path as the debtor's.

fields.name: Creditor Account
fields.note: Where the money lands.

fields.name: Ultimate Debtor
fields.note: The party the payment is ultimately on behalf of, when that differs from the account holder. Used for payment-service-provider and on-behalf-of flows; sanctions screening cares about it.

fields.name: Ultimate Creditor
fields.note: The final beneficiary when the credited account belongs to someone else, e.g. a collection agent.

fields.name: Instruction For Creditor Agent
fields.note: Coded plus free-text instructions for the creditor agent, e.g. PHOB to telephone the beneficiary. The MT 72 equivalent.

fields.name: Purpose
fields.note: For the creditor's benefit. Agents must pass it through untouched and must not route on it.

fields.name: Proprietary Purpose
fields.note: A non-ISO purpose code agreed bilaterally or domestically. Where legacy MT field 26T values land when they are not ISO external purpose codes.

fields.name: Regulatory Reporting
fields.note: Balance-of-payments and central-bank reporting detail required by some jurisdictions.

fields.name: Related Remittance Information
fields.note: Pointer to remittance detail sent separately — the link to a remt.001.

fields.name: Remittance Information
fields.note: What the payment is for, so the creditor can reconcile it. Choose structured or unstructured — ISO permits both, but most schemes allow only one.

fields.name: Unstructured Remittance Information
fields.note: Free text, 140 characters per occurrence. Repeating in base ISO, but CBPR+ and SEPA both cap it at a single occurrence — so assuming you can send 4 x 140 characters is a portability trap.

fields.name: Structured Remittance Information
fields.note: Machine-readable invoice and reference detail. Far better for automated reconciliation, far less widely supported.

fields.name: Referred Document Information
fields.note: Invoice type, number and date.

fields.name: Referred Document Amount
fields.note: Due amount, discounts, credit notes and the remitted amount.

fields.name: Creditor Reference Information
fields.note: A structured reference issued by the creditor — e.g. an ISO 11649 RF reference or a Swiss QR reference.

fields.name: Supplementary Data
fields.note: The standard's official escape hatch for scheme-specific extensions. Anything here is by definition non-portable.
